checks.claim: Grid convergence at alpha 4 deg: CL 0.4557 / 0.4495 / 0.4929 on 622,283 / 1,795,211 / 4,592,028 tetrahedra.
assumptions: the three meshes share every sizing rule (one scale factor)

reproduced.how: computed here from the stored coefficients

CMy.note: oscillatory or zero change: no asymptotic estimate

checks.status_reason: GCI_fine on CL not computable: oscillatory or zero change: no asymptotic estimate; CMy oscillatory or zero change: no asymptotic estimate
limitations: discretisation error only; model error (inviscid) is separate

checks.claim: SU2's reported forces equal an independent pressure integration over the same wall triangles.
equations: F = -sum_i p_i n_i A_i (n into the fluid, from the owning tetrahedron)
assumptions: node pressures averaged to triangle centroids (SU2 uses the same nodal dual-area idea, so small differences are expected)
checks.ran_evidence: post-processing reads restart_flow.csv written by SU2
limitations: checks bookkeeping (reference area, axes, moment centre), not the flow solution

checks.claim: Boundary conditions behave: no flow through the symmetry plane; free stream recovered at the far field.
assumptions: domain 8 m ahead, 16 m behind, 8 m above/below, 10 m to the side of the half model
checks.ran_evidence: read from the SU2 restart files

independent_check.method: nodal velocities on the marker nodes

checks.status_reason: |v_y|/V <= 4.0e-16 on the symmetry plane; far-field |V|/V in 0.999-1.000

equations: CL = CL0 + CL_alpha alpha (least squares, |alpha| <= 6 deg)
Helmbold: a = a0 / (sqrt(1 + (a0/(pi AR))^2) + a0/(pi AR))
assumptions: Helmbold is wing-only (no tail, pod or booms)
AVL: vortex lattice + slender pod, same CG

independent_check.method: AVL (pod) lift slope; Helmbold wing-only as a sanity bound

checks.status_reason: CFD 4.42 vs AVL 5.26 /rad (-16.1 %); Helmbold wing alone 5.30; the gap matches the under-resolution the 2-D check measures at this wall spacing (CFD-12), so the CFD slope is a lower bound, not evidence against AVL
limitations: AVL and CFD share the planform and CG but not the solver or the body model; AVL geometry is one sizing pass older (chord 281.8 vs 284.2 mm)

checks.claim: CL 0.493 at alpha 4 deg, elevator 0, V 18 m/s (finest mesh).
assumptions: inviscid: no boundary-layer decambering, so CFD should sit a few % above a viscous answer

independent_check.method: AVL 3.52 with pod at the same alpha and elevator

checks.status_reason: -4.1 % against AVL on the finest mesh (L3); CL on L1/L2/L3 0.4557, 0.4495, 0.4929 is not monotone, so the agreement is not yet grid-independent

checks.claim: Neutral point 42.3 % MAC from the CFD moment slope (static margin 14.3 % at the 28 % CG).
assumptions: moment centre at the design CG on the chord line
limitations: power-off; propeller normal force and slipstream not modelled
checks.next_step: Flight: trim-elevator-vs-speed test for the stick-fixed neutral point (test plan).

checks.claim: Induced drag from the Trefftz plane CDi 0.0097 at alpha 4 deg.
equations: CDi = (2/(q S)) * integral of 1/2 rho (v^2 + w^2) dA over the half plane
assumptions: far-field kinetic-energy form; streamwise perturbation neglected

independent_check.method: CL^2/(pi e AR) with AVL's span efficiency

checks.status_reason: Trefftz 0.0097 on the plane 0.3 m behind the wing TE vs CL^2/(pi e AR) 0.0095 (+1 %); planes further aft read 0.0089, 0.0080 as the trailing vortices dissipate on the tetrahedra, so the value depends on where it is measured
limitations: numerical dissipation of the trailing vortices before the plane
plane truncated at 4 m x 4 m

checks.claim: The inviscid solver's surface CD (0.0371) is not a drag prediction.
assumptions: no skin friction, no physical separation in an Euler run

evidence.what: the viscous drag the sizing uses

checks.status_reason: surface CD minus the Trefftz CDi is numerical (blunt clamp and motor bases, coarse tetrahedra); profile drag stays with analysis/aero/drag_buildup.py
limitations: a viscous (RANS) full-aircraft run with prism layers is needed for drag
checks.next_step: Car-roof / flight power test (aero M1, mass M3) remains the drag evidence.

checks.claim: Surface pressure stays within the incompressible stagnation bound (Cp <= 1) everywhere on the aircraft.
checks.units: Cp max on a wall node
assumptions: nodal values from the restart file
checks.ran_evidence: read from the SU2 restart files
checks.status_reason: 2.41 on the htail (L2_a8.0); L1_a4.0: 2615 wall nodes above 1, L2_a0.0: 1938 wall nodes above 1, L2_a2.0: 2201 wall nodes above 1, L2_a4.0: 1846 wall nodes above 1, L2_a6.0: 1839 wall nodes above 1, L2_a8.0: 1872 wall nodes above 1, L3_a4.0: 1066 wall nodes above 1. Stagnation overshoot where the 0.9 mm horizontal-tail leading-edge radius and sharp box corners are resolved by only 1-2 mm elements
limitations: local: the integrated tail load is a small share of CL, but tail-LE pressures from this run must not be used
checks.next_step: Refine the tail and fin leading edges (curvature sizing below 0.3 mm) and re-run; check the overshoot falls with refinement.

checks.claim: At the wall spacing of the 3-D meshes, the SU2 scheme reproduces the inviscid lift of the wing section.
equations: same SU2 INC_EULER numerics as run_cases.CFG on a 2-D gmsh mesh of the same NACA 2415 section
assumptions: 2-D section behaviour carries over to the 3-D wing's chordwise resolution
checks.ran_evidence: SU2 and XFOIL run by analysis/cfd3d/scheme_check_2d.py (2000+ iterations per case)
checks.status_reason: at the L1/L2 wall spacing the section lift slope is -19 / -14 % against XFOIL inviscid; it closes to -5 % at 603 wall edges. Numerical dissipation at this resolution acts like viscous decambering, which explains most of the 3-D lift-slope gap to AVL (CFD-05): absolute lift from the 3-D runs is mesh-limited
checks.next_step: Re-mesh the wing, tail and fins at about 2 mm wall spacing (about 300 wall edges per section) and re-run alpha 0, 4, 8; keep the other parts at the current sizes.

checks.claim: Cruise chord Reynolds number 3.46e+05: attached, lift-dominated flow, so inviscid CFD is admissible for lift and moment at alpha <= 8 deg.
equations: nu = mu/rho, mu 1.81e-5 Pa s (ISA 15 C)

independent_check.method: XFOIL section at Re 3.5e5 stays attached to ~10 deg (aero_results.json section_polars)

checks.status_reason: Re matches the aero package (AERO-01); attached-flow range from the viscous section polar
limitations: laminar separation bubbles at Re 3.5e5 are not represented
